subject: Request: short-term response-capacity stretch & escalation path for GreenByte maintenance
messages:
From: Patrick Nguyen <patrick.nguyen@greenbyte.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@greenbyte.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned maintenance week — ask about temporary SLA flexibility

Hi Marissa,

GreenByte will be running a coordinated data-center migration and scheduled maintenance from May 15–18 (US PST). We expect higher-than-normal traffic and a smaller on-site postmortem team on our side that week. We wanted to check whether Redwood can offer a short-term tweak to our support response commitments for that period — specifically:

- Relax P2 response from 4 hours to 8 hours for the 48-hour window starting 2028-05-15T00:00 PDT (only for non-customer-impacting maintenance alerts).
- Confirm that P1 (system-down) remains at the contracted 1-hour response with prioritized escalation.

We are open to signing a short addendum if you can provide an internal on-call augmentation or an explicit fallback escalation path during the migration. Attached is our maintenance plan for reference.

Thanks — Patrick
Patrick Nguyen
Head of Platform Ops, GreenByte Finance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Patrick Nguyen <patrick.nguyen@greenbyte.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@greenbyte.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance week — ask about temporary SLA flexibility

Thanks for the heads-up, Patrick — the plan looks straightforward. Ben / Karthik: can we support a temporary P2 response extension (4h -> 8h) limited to the specified 48-hour window and scoped to maintenance-only alerts? Key constraints from legal/SRE I expect: no change to P1, explicit rollback if customer-impacting incidents occur, and a signed addendum.

Suggested mitigations we can offer if we approve:
- Redwood to designate a primary escalation (Ben) and a secondary (Soojin) for P1s during the window.
- Create a short-term on-call shadow for P2s staffed by our Dedicated Support pool (overnight augmentation).
- Add a clause in the addendum requiring immediate reversion to standard SLA if cumulative P1/P2 outages exceed thresholds.

I'll draft the SLA amendment and attach it for review. Patrick, once we have internal sign-off, we can push a DocuSign link.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Patrick Nguyen <patrick.nguyen@greenbyte.com>
Date: Tue, 01 May 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance week — ask about temporary SLA flexibility

On Tue, May 1, 2028 at 10:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads-up, Patrick — the plan looks straightforward. Ben / Karthik: can we support a temporary P2 response extension (4h -> 8h) limited to the specified 48-hour window and scoped to maintenance-only alerts?

We can — I’ve checked capacity for the Dedicated Support pool and we can add a single overnight shadow (US PST) for the 48-hour maintenance window. Conditions:

- P1 remains unchanged (1 hour).
- The P2 extension is explicitly limited to alerts that GreenByte labels as "maintenance-only" (we need a short ticketing tag filter).
- If any incident escalates beyond maintenance category, Redwood will revert to standard SLA and triage immediately.

Escalation path for P1s during the window:
1) On-call support (primary) — Ben Carter (call, Slack escalation)
2) Secondary — Soojin Lee (phone & EMER hotline)
3) Head of CS — Marissa Cole (if unresolved > 30m)

I can own the DocuSign signature line for the Redwood side once the addendum is finalized. Approving the draft below is fine from my side.

-Ben
Senior Manager, Support Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Patrick Nguyen <patrick.nguyen@greenbyte.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@greenbyte.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 May 2028 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: SLA addendum draft for GreenByte maintenance (attached)

Patrick / Laura —

Attached is Redwood's proposed short addendum that implements the two changes we discussed: temporary P2 response extension limited to maintenance-only alerts and the explicit escalation path for P1s. Highlights:
- Effective window: 2028-05-15T00:00 PDT through 2028-05-17T23:59 PDT (48 hours).
- P2: 4h -> 8h for maintenance-only alerts only.
- P1: unchanged (1h). Immediate reversion clause included.
- Contact & escalation list included (Ben = primary, Soojin = secondary, Marissa = CS head).

Next steps:
1) GreenByte: confirm the ticket-tag filter name you will use for "maintenance-only" events so our routing can respect it.
2) We will update the addendum with your preferred tag and send a DocuSign link for signatures.
3) Redwood will schedule the overnight Dedicated Support shadow and share a brief runbook with the contact numbers.

Please review and let me know by EOD tomorrow if that timeline works — we need ~7 business days to stand up the shadow and complete the ticket-rule test.

Best,
Marissa

From: Patrick Nguyen <patrick.nguyen@greenbyte.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@greenbyte.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA addendum draft for GreenByte maintenance (attached)

Marissa — thanks, team. GreenByte approves the proposed language with one item: our ops team will tag maintenance-only alerts with the ticket label "GB-Maintenance" (we'll add a rapid test ticket this week so you can validate routing).

We agree to the reversion clause. Please go ahead and send the DocuSign when you're ready — aiming to have signatures by Wednesday so the shadow can be stood up.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

—Patrick
